A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VC-Inspector work. All 12 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark correlations, training ablations, runtime measurements and explanation-quality evaluations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds CAPability caption-refinement experiments and human evaluation of generated explanations.

M1.justification: V1 Section 4.2 fine-tunes the vision-language merger alongside LLM LoRA parameters; v2 Section 3.3 and Table 9 freeze the projector and fine-tune only LLM LoRA parameters. V2 also introduces an iterative caption-refinement application using evaluator feedback. The core synthesis pipeline, loss and evaluator outputs remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V2 adds CAPability evaluation of caption refinement across 12 image/video tasks, including camera movement, object properties, OCR and style. This substantially extends coverage from judging caption quality to improving generated captions. The original ActivityNet, YouCook2, VATEX and Flickr8K coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets are retained. V2 Tables 6 and 8 introduce no-feedback caption generation and off-the-shelf Qwen2.5-VL-7B feedback as controls against VC-Inspector feedback in the new refinement experiment.

E3.justification: V2 adds an up-to-ten-iteration refinement protocol with a fixed Qwen2.5-VL-7B captioner, GPT-4.1 grading and F1 reporting. It also adds Likert ratings of explanations for 100 randomly sampled VATEX captions by three authors. The stated projector-freezing configuration changes, while existing benchmark splits and correlation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Section 4.4 adds tests of explanation usefulness for caption refinement and direct human assessment of explanation quality. Existing synthesis/explanation ablations and automatic explanation evaluation are retained. V1's two-caption factual-error probe in Table 1 and two-run stability analysis are removed. The qualitative examples are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: V1's two-run Pearson stability check is removed. V2 newly reports human-rating standard deviation of 0.8, ordinal Krippendorff's alpha of 0.46 and 85.4% agreement within one point. This adds annotation-variability reporting, without introducing repeated-seed uncertainty estimates for the principal benchmark results.

E6.justification: V1 Tables 2–6 retain their numerical results as v2 Tables 1–5; automatic explanation scores and runtime values also remain. V2 adds CAPability results: average F1 is 51.5 with VC-Inspector feedback, 51.1 without feedback and 36.8 with Qwen feedback, with declines versus no feedback on five dimensions. Human explanations receive a mean rating of 4.33. V1's diagnostic Table 1 scores and Pearson 1.0 stability result are removed.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.2 explicitly defines integer-score discretization as round(4s + 1), whereas v1 only states conversion into the 1–5 range. This is a limited addition to the mathematical specification. The fractional factual-error score, sampling definitions and underlying reasoning remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V2's abstract, introduction and conclusion newly claim that explanatory feedback can guide caption improvement. This extends the original evaluation and interpretability contributions. The central claims about reference-free factual evaluation, synthetic training data and cross-domain benchmark performance are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations that factual/explanation supervision matters more than model scale and that unsuitable feedback can damage captions. Its limitations newly address synthetic errors' incomplete representation of real-world errors and multimodal computational costs. V1 mainly discussed extending beyond object/action errors to attributes and temporal or narrative properties.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands reproducibility information: 32-frame 224×224 preprocessing, one training epoch, cosine scheduling and warmup, and runtime measurement over 2,000 videos with 16 frames and vLLM serving. It adds a project-page URL, refinement prompt and consolidated hyperparameter table. These are mostly new disclosures, not demonstrated setting changes. Table 2 also clarifies that CLAIR and PAC-S scores come from their original papers.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for CAPability, vLLM/PagedAttention and Spathis and Kawsar's numerical-representation discussion, while removing LITA and Xiao et al.'s evaluation-metric framework citation. The principal positioning against text-based, embedding-based and proprietary evaluators remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and related work, consolidates v1's separate task-overview and instruction-tuning sections into Methodology, and reorganizes explanation analyses. It adds a separate Limitations section and restructures the appendices, moving prompts from Appendix A to D and qualitative results to Appendix A.

P2.justification: V2 changes page geometry, typography and table sizing, including author-year labels in compact comparison tables. It removes v1's diagnostic Table 1 and adds refinement Tables 6/8 and hyperparameter Table 9. V1 Figure 4 moves to appendix Figure 5, while appendix Figure 5 becomes main-text Figure 4. Prompt boxes and other retained displays are extensively rearranged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility and baseline provenance, and supplements v1's synthetic explanation evaluation with human ratings and a controlled refinement experiment. These provide useful additional support for explanation quality and utility. The gain remains limited: human raters are authors, refinement improves average F1 only from 51.1 to 51.5 with several task declines, and the principal benchmark results are unchanged.
